notes: Loop 2 re-check (loop 1: 7.8). I checked the phone, desktop and dark screenshots of the landing page, the German report (plus the EN, ES and PL text), slider-moved, /try and connect-beta. All five loop-1 items are fixed. The rehearsal tells a story: 4 noticed, 2 tried, 3 told, and Jan→Chiara matches the landing teaser. Step 2 is folded, and the phone report is 11,763 px against 23,943. Every 'Warum sich das geändert hat' sum checks (−117,70 € → −118 €; at 11 a day, +42,80 €). The hero and the six steps match the report, and the chips sit beside the right things. New and strong: 'Wer hat was gemacht?' as the first card, a guess before the reveal in step 4, the after-test chart, correct German number formats, no English left in DE, ES or PL, and a calm dark mode. Held back: three pairs of interview answers are word-for-word identical (report.txt:481/505, 487/493, 499/511), so the most original feature looks canned. A /try report ends step 5 with 'Bitten Sie Ihren KI-Coach' for people who have none. Step 4's 'one number' is really two (11 and 7). The landing page says 'Gewinnschwelle', the report 'Break-even'. No cap applies.
improvements: Report step 5, the interview (src/report/demo.ts withInterview, the rule-based interview lines in src/sim/messages.ts; report.txt:476-511): no two imagined customers may give the same answer. Today Noor and Greta, Chiara and Paweł, and Murat and Jan each say identical sentences, and the desktop view shows them expanded. Build each answer from that persona's own details (her quirk, her usual alternative, her budget: Noor's nut question, Paweł's €7.90), or group the duplicates ('Noor und Greta: …'), or use the Claude-played run's interview. Why: the rehearsal is the most original visual, and copy-paste answers make the neighbourhood look like a template. Done when report.txt has 6 distinct interview answers in every language.

A /try report, step 5 (src/report/rehearsal.ts:216-219, src/report/messages.ts:750): replace the empty state 'Bitten Sie Ihren KI-Coach: …' with a button that runs the rule-based rehearsal in the browser for that report, labelled 'einfache feste Regeln, keine KI'. /try is the page for owners without an AI app, so the step ends in a dead end exactly for its audience. Why: hands-on learning, and the stepper in try-done-report.png stays at '4 von 6 fertig' with a dashed step 5. Done when a /try report can show the persona grid and reach 6 von 6.

Report step 4, 'Die Zahl zum Merken' (src/report/sections.ts step4; report.txt:246-298): the step promises one number and shows two ('Break-even: 11', 'Trägt sich: 7'). The keep rule uses 7, and the short answer uses 11. Make the order visible in one caption under the chart: '11 = der Test spielt seine Startkosten wieder ein · 7 = ab da trägt sich jeder weitere Tag (die Startkosten sind schon ausgegeben)'. Also note why the line crosses 0 € at about 10.2 while the marker sits at 11 ('aufgerundet auf ganze Gäste'). Why: a judge or owner skimming on a phone should leave with one number and its twin explained, not two competing ones. Done when the chart caption names both and the rounding.

German wording, landing page against report (site/src/messages.ts; landing.txt:138-142 'Gewinnschwelle: 11 pro Tag' against report.txt:38, :246-248, :282, :588 'Break-even'): use one term. Introduce it once as 'Break-even (Gewinnschwelle)' and keep it the same on the landing page, in the stepper, in the chart label and in 'Nutzen Sie die Methode wieder'. Why: the landing page teaches a word that the report never uses, on the very number it asks the owner to remember. Done when the German landing page and report use the same word for step 4.

After-test demo and the UI evidence (/r#demo-result, src/report/sections.ts step 6 result; qa/ui-check.ts): the result bars read 'Gemessen (gemessen)', and the measured 6 a day wears an 'Ihre Zahl' chip in a demo. Write 'Gemessen' once, and use the 'Demo-Daten' chip when analysis.demo is set. The UI bot also takes no screenshot of /r#demo-result, the page that best shows the learning loop. Add report-result-phone.png so judges and the QA loop see it. Done when the screenshot exists and shows one label for each bar.
pitchIn60s: Visually it is a lesson, not a dashboard, and now in four languages. It opens with 'who did what' (demo data, calculated by code, guesses, imagined, and what the AI did). You guess the break-even before it is shown, and the slider's chart, readout and 'why this changed' sentence move together and add up to the cent. The worst case is drawn against spare cash. A living imagined-Kiez grid shows who tried it and who told whom, then come a one-page printable test card and an after-the-test chart that puts reality on the line with your guesses. It works on a phone and in dark mode, with German number formats throughout. Small blemishes remain: canned duplicate interview answers, a dead end in step 5 for /try users, and two break-even numbers where the step promises one.
standout: Step 4's guess-first-then-slider. 'Bevor Sie hinsehen: Schätzen Sie selbst' hides the answer. Then one drag moves the line, the marker, the euro readout and a 'Warum sich das geändert hat' sentence whose sum checks by hand (11 × 5,35 € − 36,57 € = 22,28 €; × 10 − 180 € = 42,80 €).
weakest: The rehearsal interview: three pairs of imagined customers give word-for-word identical answers (report.txt:481/505, 487/493, 499/511), which undercuts an otherwise lively persona grid.
